page: Amazon Web Services r8a.4xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated physical cores utilizing the x86_64 AMD EPYC 9R45 processor, operating at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The CPU architecture includes 48 KB L1d, 1.0 MB L2, and 32 MB L3 cache per core, supporting advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, AVX-VNNI, and AES cryptography. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 6 GHz, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per core. No local storage or GPUs are included in this configuration, and network connectivity is rated at an 8 Gbps baseline.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core, Geekbench single-core, and single-threaded gzip compression all placing in the top 10%. Multi-core execution is solid, with Geekbench multi-core scoring in the top 10% and stress-ng multi-core landing in the middle 50%. Memory performance is strong, as evidenced by a top 25% PassMark memory score and stable read/write bandwidths. For specialized workloads, the instance achieves top-tier results in image processing, text processing, and small-model LLM inference, while maintaining average performance for software compilation, ray tracing, and database operations.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8:1 and DDR5 architecture, the r8a.4xlarge provides qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound workloads that do not require local NVMe storage. The dedicated core allocation ensures predictable execution without resource contention. This profile is highly suitable for memory-intensive applications, including in-memory databases, caching layers like Redis, data processing pipelines, and small-scale language model inference.
